children: U.S. services-sector activity continued to expand last month, maintaining a 26-month streak, a survey of managers found.

The Institute for Supply Management's purchasing managers index for services providers was 55.4 in August compared with 54.1 in July. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expected the reading to hold steady month-over-month. A reading above 50 suggests economic growth, while one below 50 indicates contraction.
The new orders index registered 60.9, up from 57.2 in July. The employment index remained in contraction territory for a second consecutive month.
The prices index registered above 70 for the fifth time in six months.
The supplier deliveries index continued to indicate slower performance, the survey said.
"Tariffs and the Middle East conflict returned as the most-cited issues impacting respondents' supply chains," said Steve Miller, chair of the ISM Services Business Survey Committee.
